changes: Short weeks are now found properly on the timesheet's hours-in-lieu box. A week with nothing recorded counts as fully short, and so does a week that runs into the next or previous month (such as the last week of October). Before, those were skipped.
A week at the month's edge is measured as a whole week, Monday to Sunday, across both months. Top it up on one month's timesheet and the other month's sheet knows.
The week you're in isn't called short until it's over, so Fill short weeks never fills a week you're still working in.
The week list now says 'short' with the amount, for example 'Week of Mon 26 Oct · 0h 00m charged · 6h 00m short'.
Hours in lieu on the timesheet: every monthly timesheet now opens with the client's banked hours and a way to add them, so you don't have to go to the area's page first.
Fill short weeks: one button tops up this month's weeks that are under the weekly hours, earliest first, until the bank runs out.
Or add your own amount: type the hours, pick a week of the month or a day, and press Add to this timesheet.
Added hours come straight out of the bank and appear below as an 'added' entry. Delete the entry to put them back.
If the month is already invoiced, the box says so instead, because that invoice can't change.

HTB now banks automatically, like your other areas. Any week over its hours a week, the extra goes into its hours in lieu and comes off that week's charge. This works for every client invoiced by the day, not just by the week.
The hours held back come off the last days worked that week. The timesheet shows them on the day: 'over the weekly hours: banked, not charged here'.
Roll over still works. An entry you roll over goes to carried hours as before and isn't banked as well. The area's hours in lieu add the two together.
The allowance line at the top of the timesheet says how much was banked automatically, and 'charging' is now what the invoice will actually charge.
Only clients with a card on the Dashboard are banked.
Phone layout fixed throughout: nothing runs off the side of the screen or scrolls sideways any more, and long sentences wrap.

Getting back from a timesheet: on a phone, timesheets, invoices and the carried hours ledger now open in the same screen with a '← Tracker' button at the top to return to where you were. On a computer they still open in a new tab.
All five tabs fit across a phone screen.
Area cards on a phone show This week and This month one above the other, so long hours fit inside the card.
Tables (timesheets, invoice lines, the ledger, Clients compared, and every Settings table) turn into a list of short blocks on a phone, each figure under its heading.

Every device now moves to a new version together. When the tracker is updated, a page left open on your phone or another computer loads the new version by itself, instead of carrying on with the old one until you refreshed it.
If you're part-way through changing a setting when that happens, it waits and shows a Reload button so nothing you've typed is lost.
Coming back to the tracker on your phone now refreshes the figures straight away, instead of waiting up to a minute.
Sync now also refreshes an area's page if you have one open. Before, its figures could lag up to a minute behind.

Hours in lieu now fill by themselves: any week you work more than an area's hours a week, the extra goes into its bank. You still choose when to use them, by adding them to a day or week on the area's page.

For a client invoiced by the week, the hours over are also left off that week's invoice (the timesheet says how many were banked) and are charged when you add them to a later day or week. Every hour is charged once.
Settings → Dashboard cards has two new columns: 'Bank hours over that' to switch it on or off for each area, and 'Counting from' for the date it starts. It starts from 01/09/2026.

The bank counts weeks in months you've already invoiced, on the understanding that those invoices charged only the hours a week. The area's page names the months it's assuming this for. If one of them charged everything you worked, move 'Counting from' to after it.
Clients with a monthly allowance (Roll over and carried hours) are left as they are. Clients invoiced by the day or by the hour can only be banked by hand.
Once a month is invoiced, what its weeks banked is fixed, so changing the hours a week later can't alter that invoice or lose banked time.
'Adjust the bank by hand' is still there for anything the automatic count misses.
Tidier Settings: every section now folds away, so the page opens as a short list. Click a heading to open it, and it stays open next time. 'Open all' at the top shows everything at once.
Sections are grouped: Dashboard, Invoicing, Time and targets, and This app.
An orange dot on a closed section's heading means it has changes you haven't saved.
Links into Settings from other pages open the right section for you.

Area cards: the top of the Dashboard now has a card for each of your main clients, showing hours this week and this month. Choose which clients have a card, and what each is called, in Settings → Dashboard cards.

Area pages: click a card for a page about that client. It shows this week, this month and last week, and a chart of hours you can switch between by day (28 days), by week (12 weeks) and by month (12 months), split by task.

Hours a week: in Settings → Dashboard cards, enter the hours you mean to do for each client every week. Each card then shows a progress bar and how much is left to do. A card turns red when you're behind for the week, and a 'Do first' line under the cards lists what to prioritise, furthest behind first, with the hours a day needed to catch up.
On an area's page, the weekly chart has a line at your allotted hours, and weeks that fell short are faded.

Hours in lieu: each area has a bank of hours you type in. Pick the day, or pick the week from a list, and the banked hours become real time: they count in your totals and go on that client's timesheet and invoice, marked as added. Delete the added entry on the timesheet and the hours go back in the bank.
For a client with a monthly allowance, the hours-in-lieu figure also includes carried-over time. You still add carried-over time from the timesheet.
Money to collect reminds you about banked hours on paying clients that haven't been used.

Carried hours ledger: a new page showing, month by month for each allowance, the max, hours worked, hours rolled over, hours added to an invoice, the balance left and its value, and whether the month is marked as invoiced. Open it from Outstanding on the Dashboard, from Settings, or from the allowance line on a timesheet. Each month links to its timesheet.
Allowances for a whole client: tick 'Bill as allowance' on a client's weekly limit and all of that client's work counts, so any of its entries can be rolled over.
Several allowances for one client: each task's allowance has its own maximum, Roll over ticks, carried-over box and balance.
A client can have allowances on its tasks or one for all its work, not both, because the same hours would count twice. Settings tells you if you try.
Your existing Justin allowance, rolled-over entries and carried hours are unchanged.
Email invoices from the app: Email it on an invoice (or Email in the Invoices list) attaches the invoice PDF and the timesheet PDF, addresses it to the client and writes the message for you.

Each business chooses how, under Settings → Your businesses → 'Email invoices with'. Apple Mail on this Mac makes a draft for you to check and send, from that business's email address. The first time, macOS asks to let the tracker control Mail: click OK.

Or use your own email provider: enter its outgoing mail server (SMTP), username and password. Invoices are then sent straight away, after you confirm, with a copy to you. The password is kept in the Mac's Keychain. Most providers need an 'app password'.
Send a test email checks a business's email setup before you rely on it.
The invoice number to start from is 'Next number' in Settings → Your businesses, one per business.

More than one business: in Settings, 'Your businesses' has '+ Add another business'. Each business has its own name, address, payment details, VAT and invoice numbers. Then choose which business invoices each client under 'Who each invoice goes to' (the 'Invoiced by' column). The details you already entered are kept as your first business.

Extras on invoices: on the Invoices tab, add extra time that wasn't on the cube, mileage (45p a mile unless you change it) or an expense for a client and month. Extras go on that client's invoice for the month, after the time lines, and are counted in what's ready to invoice.
Removing an extra, or voiding an invoice, puts things back: a voided invoice's extras are ready for the next one.
Invoices now say Quantity instead of Hours, so miles and expenses read properly.

Invoices made in the app: a new Invoices tab lists every finished month ready to invoice. Create invoice makes a numbered invoice with your details, the client's details, VAT if you're registered, the due date and how to pay. Save it as a PDF or print it.

First, fill in Settings: 'Your business' (name, address, how clients pay you, VAT, and the next invoice number so it carries on from your old ones) and 'Who each invoice goes to' (each client's name, address, email and payment terms).
Create all invoices: one button makes every invoice that's ready, then offers them in one ZIP with the matching timesheet PDFs.

Each invoice page has Email it (a ready-written email to the client: attach the saved PDF), Save timesheet PDF, Mark as paid and Void. An invoice is a fixed copy and never changes. Void one that's wrong and create it again: the number isn't reused.
Creating an invoice marks the month as invoiced. Money to collect then chases it by its own due date and total, including VAT.
Monthly timesheets have a Create invoice button at the top. Mark as invoiced and the Copy buttons still work if you invoice somewhere else.

Reports now opens with your earnings: tax year to date, monthly average, this month so far and average per paid hour; a chart of what you earned each month by client; clients compared by hours, income and pay per hour; your average working week; and 'What the numbers say', which points out things like your lowest-paying client and how much tracked time earns nothing.

Money to collect: a new panel at the top of the Dashboard. It lists what to do to get paid, most urgent first, with what each item is worth: months to invoice, invoices to chase, and things worth a second look.

Mark as paid: on an invoiced timesheet or in Money to collect. Unpaid invoices show as awaiting payment, then as overdue once your payment terms have passed (30 days unless you change 'Clients pay within' in Settings). If you have old invoices that were paid long ago, use 'Mark all as paid' once.

Missed money prompts: time added after you invoiced, carried hours not yet charged, excluded time on invoices that haven't gone out, working days with nothing tracked, and falling behind the pace for this month's targets.
Press Hide on a prompt you've dealt with. It comes back only if the figures change. 'Show hidden' brings them all back.

Phone and other computers (Settings): share this tracker privately with your own devices through Tailscale. Your phone and other Mac open the same live tracker, with the same data, and nothing is copied.

Bring in another Mac's changes: download a changes file on one Mac and add it on the other. Edits, added entries, exclusions, roll-overs, carried hours, invoiced marks and settings are merged in. Nothing on the receiving Mac is overwritten, and it reports anything both Macs did differently.

Viewer mode: your other Mac's TimeFlip Tracker app can open the main Mac's tracker instead of its own. It stops syncing and alerting on its own, and its data is backed up first. 'Stop being a viewer' undoes it.
Timesheets now fit a phone screen, and there's an orange clock icon for your phone's Home Screen.

Mark as invoiced: a button at the top of each monthly timesheet. It records the date with the hours and amount at the time, and Undo reverses it. If the timesheet changes afterwards, it warns 'Changed since'.
Outstanding on the Dashboard now lists every month not yet marked as invoiced (in red, with a 'Mark invoiced' button), as well as this month so far and carried hours.
Earlier months are counted from the first month you mark as invoiced for each client. Until then, last month is shown.

New Outstanding strip at the top of the Dashboard. For each client it shows this month's hours still to invoice and their value, plus hours carried over but not yet charged (e.g. Justin's) and their value, with totals.
Each client card has a link straight to that client's timesheet for the month.

The hours chart has a period menu: this week, last week, this month, last month, or tax year to date (from 6 April). Weeks show days, months show weeks, and the tax year shows months. Your choice is remembered.
Carried-over hours: Justin entries ticked Roll over now go into a carried-over balance instead of being charged automatically the next month. Hours brought in from Settings join the same balance.
On any later HTB timesheet, the carried-over box shows the balance with buttons: Fill spare weeks, +15m, +30m, +1h, Add all, −15m and Clear. Whatever you don't add stays for later.
Fill spare weeks adds as much as fits in the weeks where Justin was under that week's max. Added hours appear as one invoice line per week, and week totals show '+ carried over'.
Anything you rolled over before this update is now in the balance, ready to add with the buttons.

By-the-week timesheets (e.g. FCY) have an 'Even out the weeks' tick box in Invoice lines. It spreads the month's total evenly over its weeks in whole blocks, with the same total; any spare block goes to the busiest week.
Each smoothed line shows the real hours underneath. The timesheet itself still shows the real week totals. Your choice is remembered for each client.

New Save PDF button on every timesheet (and on the Timesheets tab). The tracker writes the PDF itself and it goes straight to your Downloads folder, with no print box, so Safari can't save a blank page.
The PDF has A4 pages with the same entries, day and week totals, crossed-out excluded entries, adjusted, added and rolled-over notes, the allowance line, and page numbers.
The old print button is now just 'Print'.
Simpler allowances: tick Roll over beside any Justin entry on the timesheet to charge it next month instead.
Rolled entries appear under 'Brought forward' at the top of next month's timesheet and in its invoice lines, where you can roll them on again.
The line at the top of the timesheet shows Justin's maximum for the month, what you're charging, what's rolling over, and whether you're over.
Week totals show Justin's hours against that week's maximum.
The week-by-week table, the Charged boxes and the Charge / Roll over buttons have been removed.
Allowance table: a 'Charged (h)' box on each week and on the brought-forward row. It shows a suggestion; type what you actually charged to replace it, or clear it to go back.
What carries into next month is the hours worked minus the hours you charged.
Charging more than was worked leaves a credit, which next month's hours use up before anything more is charged.
Charging less in one week leaves room in the allowance for later weeks that month.
The table stays open after you change something.
Allowances are now part of Limits: tick 'Bill as allowance' on a task's weekly limit, then choose the month it starts from and any hours brought in. Your existing allowance has moved across.
Limits now have a full-width box in Settings.
The allowance box on the timesheet opens into a week-by-week table showing each week's maximum, Justin's hours, over or under, and the running balance.
Spare hours in a quiet week still take up a busy week's extra hours. For a week that's over, choose Roll over (the default) or Charge to bill that week's extra hours this month.
Printed timesheets show the table with your choices, without the buttons.

Monthly allowances (Settings): cap a task, such as Justin, at so many hours a week. Each month's allowance is the weekly hours shared across its working days, so a week split across two months is shared by its weekdays.
England and Wales bank holidays (downloaded from gov.uk) don't count as working days.
Hours over a month's allowance carry into the next month with room. The timesheet notes them, and the invoice lines include a 'brought forward' line.
You can enter hours brought in from before the allowance starts.
HTB timesheets show a total for each week, with Justin's hours that week.
The dashboard shows this month's allowance: hours used, hours left, and anything carrying over.
New design: a dashboard of small tiles instead of full-width sections, with tabs for Dashboard, Reports, Timesheets and Settings.
Today tile shows your hours, a strip of when you worked (with a marker for now), money earned and own-business value.
Earned today, this week and this month tiles each show progress to their target, plus hours this week.
This week chart: hours per day, coloured by client. Targets and limits sit together in one tile.
This month shows one card per client; monthly income is entered on its card.
Targets: set income targets per day, week and month, and time targets per client (e.g. FYPTD hours per week) in Settings. Progress shows in a new Targets section.
Income targets count real money only. FYPT1 counts as an estimate from last month (its income, and its per-hour rate for days and weeks) until you enter the month's actual income.
The daily target is weekdays only unless you tick “Daily target on weekends too”; weekend earnings still show.
Fixed: saving limits or “Tasks not counted” no longer clears hourly rates you've typed but not yet saved.
The invoicing settings now say “Unsaved changes” until you click Save invoicing settings.
Settings → Tasks not counted: tick sides such as breaks, timers or “off” to leave them out of Today, charts, limits, This month and timesheets.
Today shows how much time wasn't counted.
New This month section: hours, money and per-hour rate for each client.
Set a client (e.g. FYPT1) to “Monthly income” in Settings, enter what it brings in, and see your effective hourly rate. The amount carries forward to later months until you change it.
Today now shows money earned from paying clients, using the hourly rates in Settings and the same rounding as your invoices.
Tick “My own business” beside a client (e.g. FYPT1, FYPTD) to give its time an imagined rate. It shows separately as own-business value and never appears on timesheets.
“Where your time went” shows the value of each client or task, with earned and own-business totals.
New Today section at the top: your total for today, time per task, and today's entries.
The settings tables now scroll sideways in a narrow window instead of spilling off the page.
Edit any entry on a timesheet: change its date, start and end times, or move it to a different task or client.
Add entries for time you didn't track on the cube, with + Add entry at the top of a timesheet.
Adjusted entries are marked “adjusted” with the original time, and added ones “added”, including on printed sheets. Back to original undoes an edit.
TimeFlip Tracker now has its own app with an orange clock icon, in your Applications folder. Open it from Launchpad or Spotlight, or drag it into your Dock.
Settings shows where the app is, with a Show in Finder button.
New look in Future You PT colours and fonts: dark header bar, orange accents, Sora headings.
Timesheets and invoice lines use the same colours.
Monthly timesheets now have an Invoice lines panel: one line per day (HTB) or per week (FCY), with Copy buttons for pasting into a Revolut Business invoice.
You can set an hourly rate for each client in Settings → How each client is invoiced, to show amounts on the invoice lines.
Updates now install automatically overnight (you can switch this off in Settings).
A “What's new” message like this one appears after each update.
Update now button, so new versions install without downloading a ZIP.
Your version number is shown in Settings, with a Check for updates button.
Monthly timesheets for clients billed by the day (HTB) or by the week (FCY), with day and week totals.
Exclude any entry you won't charge for. It stays on the sheet, crossed out, and isn't counted.
Each day's total can be rounded to 15-minute blocks.
